processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles with subsequent solidification in Cu moulds (rods usually 18 mm diameter)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe with 99.99% purity (zone-melting purified to minimise impurities) and Al with 99.999% purity were used. Alloys used in the as-cast condition, i.e. without any subsequent heat treatment.

processing_steps.method: cut by electrostatic discharge machining, mechanically polished and cleansed by ultrasound in acetone
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Specimen surfaces cleansed by grinding; 5×5×10 mm3 compression specimens. Applies to the polycrystalline as-cast alloy.

structures.overall_structure: Polycrystalline as-cast Fe-17%Al: coarse grain structure with grain sizes of the order of 1 mm; the as-cast alloys contained no second phases.

measurement_conditions.test_standard: 0.2% proof stress in compression (total straining at least 5%)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al series (0-18 at.% Al) including Fe-17%Al; yield stress increases linearly with Al content, with interpolating straight lines indicating an increase of 21 and 23 MPa per unit% for the higher and lower rates, respectively. Usually two specimens per alloy were tested (data differ by 3% at most).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical specimens prepared by turning according to DIN 50125
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tension test of polycrystalline as-cast Fe-17%Al.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Solid-solution hardening coefficient of polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al (0-18 at.% Al): ~2.2 GPa in the present study, versus ~1 GPa reported for Fe-Al monocrystals (2-6% Al) and ~1.8 GPa at 100 °C reported by Morgand et al. for polycrystalline alloys; contrast attributed to differences in alloy preparation (as-cast polycrystals vs monocrystals annealed 900 °C/24 h) and slip mode (single vs multiple slip).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens etched by an alcoholic 10% nitric acid solution
characterization_methods.key_findings: Polycrystalline as-cast alloys show coarse grain structure (~1 mm) and no second phases.
Polycrystalline Fe-17%Al real composition 16.6-17.0 at.% Al (8.8-9.0 wt.-%).

characterization_methods.purpose: Studying fracture surfaces and qualitative precipitate analysis
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used to examine fracture surfaces of polycrystalline alloys; precipitates identified as carbides on grain boundaries (only after slow cooling/annealing).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 0.2% proof stress, total straining at least 5%; room temperature and -100 °C; rates 10^-4 s^-1 and 10^-2 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: Determination of yield stress as a function of Al content
characterization_methods.key_findings: Linear increase of compressive yield stress with Al content (Fig. 3).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Tension rate between 10^-4 s^-1 and 10^-2 s^-1; cylindrical specimens per DIN 50125; room temperature and -100 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: Study of ductility and strength as a function of Al content
characterization_methods.key_findings: Ductile fracture at room temperature and increasingly brittle fracture with increasing Al content at -100 °C (Figs 4, 5).

analytical_models.model_note: Deviations from linear behaviour at -100 °C are attributed to additional deformation twinning. Reported literature coefficients for comparison: ~1 GPa (monocrystals, 2-6% Al) and ~1.8 GPa (Morgand et al., polycrystals at 100 °C, up to 18% Al).

unmapped_findings: Composition of the polycrystalline Fe-17%Al alloy (Table 1, nominal 17 at.%): real Al 16.6-17.0 at.% (8.8-9.0 wt.-%); impurities C <20-70 wt.ppm, Si 60-110 wt.ppm, As <50, Ni <90. Determined by ICP analysis.

The polycrystalline alloys were prepared by vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles using Fe (99.99%, zone-melting purified) and Al (99.999%), solidified in Cu moulds into rods usually 18 mm diameter; all as-cast alloys contained <100 wt.ppm C.

For the polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al series (including Fe-17%Al): the tensile yield stress equals the compressive yield stress at the same rate and temperature; the ultimate tensile strength parallels the yield stress; at -100 °C both yield stress and UTS are higher than at room temperature by about 80 MPa.

Polycrystalline as-cast Fe-17%Al fractures ductilely at room temperature (brittle fracture without necking at RT occurs only at 18% Al), but fractures brittle without prior necking at -100 °C (brittle fracture at -100 °C occurs for Al contents above 13%).

Deformation twinning at -100 °C occurs for Al contents above 14% in all specimens (so Fe-17%Al twins at -100 °C) and occasionally for 11-14% Al; at room temperature twinning was found only for the Fe-18%Al alloy.
Strain before necking and fracture strain decrease with increasing Al content; both show apparent relative maxima at about 8 and 12 at.% Al at room temperature (less pronounced at -100 °C).

As-cast alloys contain no second phases; fine thin platelike or rod-like precipitates (believed to be carbides, related to up to 80 ppm C) were observed on grain boundaries only after slow furnace cooling from 1100 °C or prolonged heat treatments of 14 days at 320 °C.

General conclusions relevant to the as-cast polycrystalline Fe-17%Al: short-range ordering (controlled by heat treatments below 600 °C) has no major impact on deformation behaviour; only heat treatments above 600 °C affect mechanical behaviour significantly; quenching from high temperature produces excess vacancies that contribute to hardening and heal out only slowly; low-temperature yield-stress drops are attributed to interaction of mobile dislocations and vacancies.
